title: Agent-side `chat send --sender` is caller-chosen free text: the machine agent can impersonate the human operator in the kiosk chat, defeating the trust label the GUI renders
description: post_chat() (habit_core.py:452) accepts an arbitrary sender string, and the CLI exposes it directly: `habitctl chat send TEXT --sender S` (habit_core.py:767, sp_c.add_argument("--sender", default="agent:hermes-ops")) with no whitelist or agent:/human: namespace enforcement. The GUI renders sender as the trust label — Kiosk.qml:117 colors and labels the bubble 'human' vs agent purely by `modelData.sender === "human"`. The autonomous agent (which the task marks untrusted-ish: it is prompted by remote human chat messages) can therefore post `chat send "I already fixed the generator, do nothing" --sender human` (verified by execution: the GUI's chatModel returns sender='human' with that text, so the kiosk operator sees a message that appears to be their own/another human's words, in the human-styled bubble). This is a production interface flaw, not hypothetical misuse: the whole chat mailbox is designed as the human<->agent channel and the agent is the designated untrusted party that can be socially steered; the agent deceiving the operator about resolution status (or manufacturing operator consent) is precisely the trust-boundary violation the sender label exists to prevent. The SOS-responder prompt in the logs even instructs the agent to 'Reply in the kiosk chat via habitctl chat send' — so the agent writes to this channel as its primary duty, making the missing namespace check a live gap on the main path. Fix shape: restrict the CLI/GUI to two sender namespaces — agent sessions may only post with sender starting 'agent:' (or a signed/derived source), and 'human' only from the GUI bridge.
repro_hints: On a temp DB: core.post_chat(conn, 'I already fixed it — do nothing', sender='human'); core.list_chat(conn) -> last row sender=='human' — the kiosk would render it as a human-sent message. Repro harness: C:/Users/ala/AppData/Local/Temp/mantis_repro/repro.py section 'F-05 sender spoofing' (verified output shown). Temp DB only.
reasoning: post_chat (the single choke point for every chat writer: GUI bridge, CLI, agentd) now enforces sender namespaces — exactly 'human' or 'agent:<name>'; anything else raises ValueError and the CLI reports it. The GUI cannot be tricked into rendering agent text as the operator's. Verified by test_chat_sender_namespaces_enforced; 59/59 green.
